heading: Stack that stays sorted
body:
A **monotonic stack** keeps elements in descending or ascending order. When pushing, **pop everything that breaks the order**.

Use it to find the **next greater/smaller** element for every index in **O(n)** instead of O(n²).

heading: How to recognize it
body:
Look for:
- Finding the **next greater/smaller** element to the right
- Temperature changes, stock spans, histogram heights
- Problems about **visibility** (buildings, people seeing sunset)
- Brute force would compare every element with all elements to its right

label: Crux · Python

q: What is the key reason a monotonic stack achieves O(n) time complexity instead of O(n²)?
options: The stack is never larger than log(n) elements
Each element is pushed and popped at most once
The while loop only runs when the stack is empty
explain: Each of the n elements is pushed once and popped at most once, giving O(n) total operations despite the nested while loop appearance.
